meta.note: Derived from emails-phrases.json. Mirrors reviews-expressions.json (moves > function > sub-function) so the sample reader needs no genre-specific code, with two differences. The top level is the REGISTER, not a rhetorical move — register is a dimension of the genre, so formal and informal carry their own function sets and a phrase never leaks across registers. And each entry adds 'frame' (the reusable lead-in, i.e. the text before the first [placeholder]) plus 'match', a ladder of literals longest-first: the frame, then any shorter prefix that actually occurs in the samples. The samples paraphrase the bank rather than quoting it, so exact-phrase matching alone finds almost nothing. Prefixes that would also open a different entry's frame, or that end on a function word, are rejected.
meta.fixedNote: Entries marked `fixed` are CONVENTIONS, not vocabulary: greetings and sign-offs are determined by the task and by each other (Dear Sir or Madam takes Yours faithfully), so offering a learner three alternatives to a greeting teaches the opposite of the rule. The phrase layer skips them; the salutation pairing lock states them instead. The distinction the reader applies: annotate what VARIES, state what does NOT.
